newsitem.title: FRANCE: French gamblers, drinkers to pay for health.
newsitem.headline: French gamblers, drinkers to pay for health.

text.p: The French National Assembly voted on Thursday to levy new taxes on gamblers, casinos, spirits and beer to help plug the welfare deficit.

It set a 3.40 percent tax on casinos' earnings from machine games, such as one-arm bandits, and a 10 percent tax on gamblers' winnings of over 10,000 francs. Casino staff in various French cities have demonstrated against the plans.
The assembly also voted to levy a 2.4 percent tax on 35 percent of the money spent on horse-racing betting.

It dropped proposals to raise taxes on wine but passed a 4.9 percent levy on spirits, adding to existing taxes on alcoholic drinks, and a nine-centime levy on the 25-centilitre (half a pint) beer bottle.
It also agreed to tax so-called "premix" bottles of alcohol and soda whose cheap prices have made them popular with teenagers, raising concern of a rise in alcoholism among young people.
The bills, part of the 1997 budget, will later go on to the Senate (upper house).
The new levies on drinks should bring in 900 million francs next year, while each of the two new taxes on gambling should collect 200 million francs.
The conservative government is battling to stop the rise in welfare spending and plug its deficit amid budget austerity to reach the criteria for the single European currency.
